strings.name: Meryl Streep
strings.summary: Meryl Streep entered stage, television and film after training in theatre. Detailed observation, voice and accent work help her portray women from different backgrounds. From Kramer vs. Kramer and Sophie’s Choice to The Devil Wears Prada, Mamma Mia! and The Iron Lady, she has moved among family drama, comedy, musicals and biography. Her long career is also connected to public discussion of women’s roles, professional opportunities and gender equality.
strings.coverageNote: Sources checked through 13 November 2026; selected chronology extends to The Devil Wears Prada 2 in May 2026. Film release years and Oscar or Emmy ceremony years are distinguished; no changing nomination total is asserted.
strings.influence.rationale: Demonstrated range across genres in films including Sophie's Choice, influencing screen acting and the portrayal of women throughout a long career.
strings.facts.fact-01.label: Birthplace
strings.facts.fact-02.label: Education
strings.facts.fact-02.value: Vassar College, 1971; MFA, Yale School of Drama, 1975
strings.highlights.highlight-01.title: Character work across genres
strings.highlights.highlight-01.text: Sophie’s Choice, The Devil Wears Prada and Mamma Mia! show varied approaches to voice, physicality and a character’s inner life.
strings.highlights.highlight-02.title: Work spanning theatre, film and television
strings.highlights.highlight-02.text: Alongside film roles, developed a sustained acting practice through television works including Holocaust and Angels in America.
strings.timeline.event-01.title: Returns to The Devil Wears Prada
strings.timeline.event-01.text: Reprised Miranda Priestly in the sequel with the principal returning cast, revisiting the character in a changed fashion-media environment.
strings.timeline.event-02.title: Receives Cannes’ honorary Palme d’Or
strings.timeline.event-02.text: Received a career honor at the opening of the 77th Cannes Film Festival, distinct from the competitive Palme d’Or for a film.
strings.timeline.event-03.title: Wins her third acting Oscar for The Iron Lady
strings.timeline.event-03.text: Won Best Actress for portraying Margaret Thatcher in the 2011 film, combining impersonation with a study of aging.
strings.timeline.event-04.title: Stars in the musical film Mamma Mia!
strings.timeline.event-04.text: Played Donna in a musical built around ABBA songs, combining singing, comic timing and a mother-daughter story.
strings.timeline.event-05.title: Portrays an editor in The Devil Wears Prada
strings.timeline.event-05.text: Used restrained speech and gesture as fashion editor Miranda Priestly, exploring workplace power and personal costs.
strings.timeline.event-06.title: Wins an Emmy for Angels in America
strings.timeline.event-06.text: Won a leading-performance Emmy for the miniseries broadcast in 2003, playing several different characters in the television adaptation.
strings.timeline.event-07.title: Stars in Sophie’s Choice
strings.timeline.event-07.text: Used language, physicality and emotion to portray a woman carrying wartime trauma, winning Best Actress the following year.
strings.timeline.event-08.title: Appears in Kramer vs. Kramer
strings.timeline.event-08.text: Played a mother amid separation and a custody dispute, receiving her first acting Oscar the following year.
strings.timeline.event-09.title: Gains recognition in film and television
strings.timeline.event-09.text: Earned her first Oscar nomination for The Deer Hunter and an Emmy for the miniseries Holocaust.
strings.timeline.event-10.title: Enters film with Julia
strings.timeline.event-10.text: Took a small role in Fred Zinnemann’s film, extending her work from New York theatre into cinema.
strings.timeline.event-11.title: Completes her Yale drama training
strings.timeline.event-11.text: Earned an MFA at the Yale School of Drama and began professional stage work in New York.
strings.timeline.event-12.title: Born in New Jersey
strings.timeline.event-12.text: Born in Summit; studied singing and acting as a young person before attending Vassar and Yale for further training.
